questions.question: People living on railway platforms, crowded market area on the main roads with heavy traffic are likely to experience-
questions.concept: Anthropogenic stress refers to stress caused by human activities and overcrowding. Living on railway platforms, crowded markets, and heavy traffic areas are all human-caused environmental stressors.

questions.question: Which of the following is not included in Sullivan basic modes theory
questions.concept: Sullivan's three modes of experience are: Prototaxic (undifferentiated, primitive), Parataxic (distorted, autistic thinking), and Syntaxic (consensual, logical). 'Pretaxic' is not a mode in Sullivan's theory.

questions.question: The leading neuroscience theories of intelligence is called
questions.concept: The Parieto-Frontal Integration Theory (P-FIT; Jung & Haier, 2007) is the leading neuroscience model of intelligence, proposing that intelligence arises from integration between parietal and frontal brain regions.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the non-parametric counterpart of ANOVA?
questions.concept: The Kruskal-Wallis test is the non-parametric equivalent of one-way ANOVA, used when the normality assumption is violated. Mann-Whitney is the non-parametric equivalent of independent t-test; Wilcoxon is for paired t-test.

questions.question: In the equation for linear regression Y= a+b X, b stands for-
questions.concept: In the regression equation Y = a + bX, 'b' is the regression coefficient (slope) representing the change in Y for each unit change in X. 'a' is the constant (Y-intercept).

questions.question: In case of normal probability curve, the graph/ curve is plotted for
questions.concept: The standard normal curve is plotted with z-scores on the x-axis and relative frequencies (probability densities) on the y-axis. This standardization allows comparison across different distributions.

questions.question: A psychologist was interested to conduct a study on gamblers. Identifying the gamblers, even with the help of police, is a challenging task. Which of the following sampling technique will be more appropriate to take up the study?
questions.concept: Snowball sampling is ideal for hidden/hard-to-reach populations like gamblers. Existing participants refer others, creating a 'snowball' effect that builds the sample from an initially small group.

questions.question: Peterson and Seligman carried out their famous work on strengths, virtues and character. This work is referred as-
questions.concept: Peterson and Seligman's (2004) classification is called the Values in Action (VIA) Inventory of Strengths. It identifies 24 character strengths under 6 core virtues.

questions.question: The situation of conflict arising upon allocation of funding to different groups is an example of conflict arising over issues of-
questions.concept: Conflicts over resource allocation (like funding) are interest-based conflicts, where groups compete for tangible resources. This contrasts with value conflicts (differences in beliefs) or structural conflicts.

questions.question: Which of the following attribute, according to Mahatma Gandhi as well as Patanjali, is an essential condition for practicing non-violence?
questions.concept: Vairagya (non-attachment/detachment) is considered essential for practicing non-violence (Ahimsa) by both Gandhi and Patanjali. Dukha means suffering, Krodha means anger (opposite of non-violence), and Utsaha means enthusiasm.

questions.question: Spreading rumours behind someone's back can most appropriately be referred as _____
questions.concept: Indirect aggression involves harming others through social manipulation, gossip, or rumor-spreading without direct confrontation. It differs from direct/physical aggression and relational aggression (which targets relationships specifically).

questions.question: One psychologist developed a questionnaire to assess the attitude towards workplace support. Which of the following will be the best way to establish construct validity of the questionnaire?
questions.concept: Factor analysis (particularly Confirmatory Factor Analysis) is the best method for establishing construct validity — it verifies whether the items cluster into the theoretically expected factors. Cronbach's alpha and KR measure reliability, not validity.

questions.question: The distribution, which is skewed to the left, has one high point and has many high scores is called
questions.concept: A negatively skewed (left-skewed) distribution has the tail on the left, a peak at the high end, and most scores concentrated at higher values. Mean < Median < Mode in negative skew.

questions.question: In order to interpret individual test scores and to calculate confidence interval, which of the following is important and necessary?
questions.concept: SEM is essential for constructing confidence intervals around individual scores. It quantifies measurement error and is calculated as SD × √(1 - reliability coefficient).

questions.question: The multitrait- multimethod design does not provide which one of the following?
questions.concept: Campbell and Fiske's (1959) MTMM matrix provides convergent validity, discriminant validity, and reliability estimates. It does not assess predictive validity, which requires correlating test scores with future criterion measures.

questions.question: In order to interpret individual test scores and to calculate confidence interval, which of the following is important and necessary?
questions.concept: SEM is essential for constructing confidence intervals around individual scores. It quantifies measurement error and is calculated as SD × √(1 - reliability coefficient). Note: This question is a duplicate of Q14 in the original paper.

questions.question: In addition to tripartite system of working memory, Baddeley, Allen and Hitch (2011) added a fourth component which is called
questions.concept: Baddeley added the Episodic Buffer as the fourth component in 2000. It integrates information from the central executive, phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, and long-term memory into unified episodes.

questions.question: The theory which is used to compare judgements or the decisions we make under uncertain conditions is called
questions.concept: Signal Detection Theory (SDT) provides a mathematical framework for analyzing decisions under uncertainty, separating perceptual sensitivity (d') from response bias/criterion (β).

questions.question: Hull's approach to theory construction is called
questions.concept: Clark Hull employed the hypothetico-deductive method, formulating formal postulates about intervening variables (drive, habit strength) and deriving testable predictions through logical deduction.

questions.question: Who among the following is not considered as a reinforcement theorist?
questions.concept: Edwin Guthrie was an S-R contiguity theorist — he believed a single pairing of stimulus and response creates learning, without need for reinforcement. Thorndike (Law of Effect), Hull (drive reduction), and Skinner (operant reinforcement) all used reinforcement concepts.

questions.question: According to which theory of emotion the Physiological reaction and the emotion are assumed to occur simultaneously?
questions.concept: Cannon-Bard theory proposes that the thalamus simultaneously sends signals to the cortex (emotional experience) and the autonomic nervous system (physiological arousal), making them independent and concurrent.

questions.question: Who is the Personality Theorist who believed that individuals are in the process of 'becoming' and nothing is predetermined?
questions.concept: Alfred Adler's Individual Psychology emphasizes the 'creative self' and rejects determinism. He argued personality is a dynamic process of 'becoming' driven by future goals (fictional finalism), not predetermined by past causes. Skinner was a radical determinist — the opposite view.

questions.question: The disorder where an extra Sex chromosome in the 23rd pair resulting in XXY producing a male with reduced masculine characteristics resulting in enlarged breasts, obesity and excessive height is called
questions.concept: Klinefelter's syndrome (47,XXY) involves an extra X chromosome in males, resulting in reduced testosterone, gynecomastia (enlarged breasts), obesity, and tall stature. Turner's syndrome (45,X) affects females.

questions.question: In the disease called Multiple Sclerosis (MS) __
options: (C) The myelin shows bumps in some places
questions.concept: Multiple Sclerosis is an autoimmune demyelinating disease where the immune system attacks and destroys the myelin sheath covering nerve fibers, disrupting nerve signal transmission.

questions.question: The functions of Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) can be described in terms of -
options: (A) Excitatory or inhibitory, involved in arousal, attention, memory
(B) Mainly excitatory, involved in arousal and mood
(C) Majorly inhibitory involved in sleep and inhibitory movement
(D) Inhibitory neural regulation, involved in pain relief
questions.correct_text: Majorly inhibitory involved in sleep and inhibitory movement
questions.concept: GABA is the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain. It reduces neuronal excitability and plays key roles in sleep regulation, anxiety reduction, and motor control. GABA deficiency is linked to anxiety disorders and seizures.

questions.question: The area responsible for interaction between frontal, temporal and motor areas in order to produce speech is called
questions.concept: Broca's area (left frontal lobe) is responsible for speech production and coordinates with motor areas, temporal regions (Wernicke's area), and other areas for fluent speech. Damage causes Broca's (expressive) aphasia.

questions.question: Which of the following are components of hardiness?
questions.concept: Kobasa's (1979) hardiness consists of the 3 C's: Control (belief in influencing events), Commitment (engagement in activities), and Challenge (viewing change as opportunity). Hardy individuals are more resilient to stress.

questions.question: One psychologist is developing a questionnaire to assess the attitude towards workplace support. Which of the following will be the best way to establish construct validity of the questionnaire?
questions.concept: Factor analysis (EFA/CFA) is the gold standard for establishing construct validity by examining whether items load on theoretically expected factors. Alpha and KR formulas measure reliability, not validity.

questions.question: The four phases of forgiveness according to Enright, Freedman and Rique includes -
questions.concept: Enright's process model of forgiveness has four phases: Uncovering (recognizing hurt), Decision (committing to forgive), Work (developing empathy/compassion), and Deepening (finding meaning in suffering).

questions.question: The first psychology department in India was formally started in 1916 by
questions.concept: Narendra Nath Sen Gupta (N.N. Sen Gupta) established the first psychology department at the University of Calcutta in 1916, marking the formal beginning of academic psychology in India.

questions.question: The different states of consciousness like wakefulness, dream, deep sleep as well as extraordinary state (turiya avastha) are described in _____
questions.concept: The Mandukya Upanishad describes four states of consciousness: Jagrat (waking), Svapna (dreaming), Sushupti (deep sleep), and Turiya (the transcendent fourth state beyond the other three).

questions.question: The five sheaths (pancha kosas) theory is explained in _____
questions.concept: The Taittiriya Upanishad describes the Pancha Kosha (five sheaths) model: Annamaya (physical), Pranamaya (vital energy), Manomaya (mental), Vijnanamaya (intellectual), and Anandamaya (bliss).

questions.question: A famous study called the 'Robber's Cave' conducted by Sherif et all in 1961 demonstrated the social behaviour known as ____
questions.concept: Sherif's Robbers Cave experiment (1961) demonstrated that equal status contact through superordinate goals reduces intergroup hostility. The resolution phase showed that bringing groups together as equals working toward shared goals (equal status contact) reduces prejudice more effectively than mere contact.

questions.question: According to social identity theory, formation of a person's identity within a particular social group is explained by the sequential process of _______.
options: (A) Social categorization, social identity and social comparison
(B) Social identity, social categorization and social comparison
(C) Social comparison, social identity and social categorization
(D) Social comparison, social categorization and social identity
questions.correct_text: Social categorization, social identity and social comparison
questions.concept: Tajfel & Turner's SIT sequence: (1) Social categorization (classifying self and others into groups), (2) Social identity (deriving self-esteem from group membership), (3) Social comparison (comparing in-group favorably with out-groups).

questions.question: The process by which one person tries to change the belief, opinion, position or course of action of another person through argument, pleading or explanation is an example of ____
questions.concept: Persuasion is the deliberate attempt to change another person's attitudes, beliefs, or behavior through communication (arguments, pleading, explanation). It is a specific form of social influence.

questions.question: Asking for a small commitment and after gaining compliance, asking for a bigger commitment is known as _____
questions.concept: The foot-in-the-door technique (Freedman & Fraser, 1966) involves getting compliance with a small request first, which increases the likelihood of agreeing to a larger subsequent request due to self-perception consistency.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a component of creativity according to Torrance?
questions.concept: Torrance's TTCT measures Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, and Elaboration. Abstractness of titles is also measured in figural forms. Verification belongs to Wallas's creative process stages, not Torrance's components.

questions.question: While Carkhuff's model describes communication skills as pre-processing skills, Ivey and Ivey call it a ____
questions.concept: Ivey and Ivey developed the Microcounseling/Micro-Skill approach, which breaks counseling into teachable units (attending, questioning, reflecting). This parallels Carkhuff's pre-processing skills but uses a more structured micro-level framework.

questions.question: A key element in all therapeutic process is the development of an effective -
questions.concept: The working alliance (Bordin, 1979) — agreement on goals, tasks, and emotional bond — is the most robust predictor of therapeutic outcomes across all therapy orientations. It is considered the common factor in all effective therapy.

questions.question: Some casual factors occurring relatively early in life may not show their effects for many years, that may contribute to a predisposition to develop a disorder. These would be considered as ______
questions.concept: Distal risk factors are early-life influences (genetic, developmental, childhood experiences) whose effects may not manifest until much later. Proximal risk factors are immediate triggers closer to disorder onset.

questions.question:
Kohlberg's stages of moral development follows-

A. Being a moral person in the eyes of others
B. Makes moral choices based on beliefs
C. Behaves appropriately to avoid punishment
D. Conflicts with moral principles and individual rights
E. Makes choices based on what is right-behaviour

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Kohlberg's stages: Stage 1 — Punishment/Obedience (C: avoid punishment) → Stage 2 — Instrumental (E: right behavior for reward) → Stage 3 — Good Boy/Nice Girl (A: moral in others' eyes) → Stage 4 — Law and Order (B: choices based on beliefs/laws) → Stage 5 — Social Contract (D: conflicts between principles and rights).

questions.question:
Arrange the following behaviours of the child as per Piaget's stages of cognitive development.

A. The child says the volume of water in a long glass is same even when it is poured into flat bowl
B. The child looks for an object in the same place where it was hidden earlier
C. The child says that the clay ball in round shape is smaller than that the one flattened right in front of her
D. The child argues that cycling gives a better exercise to hip muscles than bending exercises by citing reasons

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: B = Sensorimotor (object permanence/deferred search). C = Preoperational (lack of conservation — flattened clay seems bigger). A = Concrete Operational (conservation of volume achieved). D = Formal Operational (abstract/hypothetical-deductive reasoning about exercise).

questions.question:
Arrange the following cognitive points sequentially to explain helping behaviour as suggested by Darley and Latane

A. Taking responsibility
B. Defining an emergency
C. Taking Action
D. Noticing
E. Planning a course of Action

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Darley and Latane's (1968) decision model for helping: (1) Notice the event (D) → (2) Define/interpret the emergency (B) → (3) Take responsibility (A) → (4) Plan a course of action (E) → (5) Take action (C). The correct sequence is D, B, A, E, C.

questions.question:
Arrange the following in the sequence of personality development propounded by psychoanalytic theory

A. Children refuse to defecate in the toilet, while some hold back the feces
B. Children enjoy breast feeding by mother and put everything in mouth
C. Children develop interest in opposite sex
D. Children are found to play with their genital organs

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Freud's psychosexual stages in order: Oral (B: breast feeding, putting things in mouth) → Anal (A: toilet training issues) → Phallic (D: genital awareness) → Latency → Genital (C: interest in opposite sex).

questions.question:
Arrange the following behaviours of a University professor in a hierarchical order as per Maslow's theory of motivation

A. Buys a two-bedroom flat
B. Attends at least one refresher course in his discipline every year
C. Applies regularly for various awards
D. Tries to maintain close relationship with the students

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Maslow's hierarchy: (A) Physiological/Safety — buying a flat (shelter) → (D) Love/Belonging — close relationships with students → (C) Esteem — applying for awards → (B) Self-actualization — professional growth through refresher courses.

questions.question:
Arrange the following stages of therapy advocated by Adler

A. Building therapeutic relationship
B. Gathering information
C. Developing new skill
D. Gaining insight

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Adlerian therapy stages: (A) Establishing the therapeutic relationship → (B) Assessment/gathering information about lifestyle → (D) Interpretation and insight into mistaken beliefs → (C) Reorientation/re-education — developing new skills and behaviors.

questions.question:
Arrange the following in a sequence as per the health belief model where an individual-

A. Reads about the various factors related to cancer
B. Stops smoking
C. Feels that since his father died of cancer he is likely to be genetically disposed
D. Understands that if he continues to smoke there is higher possibility of his suffering from cancer

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: HBM sequence: (C) Perceived susceptibility (genetic predisposition) → (D) Perceived severity (understanding risk from smoking) → (A) Perceived benefits (gathering information) → (B) Taking action (behavior change). The Health Belief Model guides behavior change through perceived threat and benefits.

questions.question:
Following are the steps that should be followed to enhance critical thinking. Arrange them in sequential order

A. Adopt the attitude of a critical thinker
B. Evaluate information sources
C. Recognize and avoid critical thinking hindrances
D. Identify and characterize arguments
E. Evaluate arguments

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Critical thinking sequence: (A) Adopt critical thinker attitude → (C) Recognize hindrances → (D) Identify/characterize arguments → (B) Evaluate information sources → (E) Evaluate arguments. This follows a disposition-first, then skills approach.

questions.question:
Cognitive psychologists and survey researchers have acknowledged that answering survey questions can be a complex cognitive task. Research suggests that when people answer survey questions, they go through four stages. Arrange the stages in order.

A. Comprehension
B. Judgement
C. Response communication
D. Retrieval

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Tourangeau's four-stage model of survey response: (A) Comprehension (understand the question) → (D) Retrieval (recall relevant information) → (B) Judgement (form an estimate/opinion) → (C) Response Communication (format and report the answer).

questions.question:
Arrange the early schools of psychology in order

A. Structuralism
B. Functionalism
C. Behaviourism
D. Humanistic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Chronological order of schools: Structuralism (Wundt, 1879) → Functionalism (James, 1890s) → Behaviorism (Watson, 1913) → Humanistic (Maslow/Rogers, 1950s-60s).

questions.question:
Read the following situations. Then order them in the sequence of nominal, ordinal, equal interval and ratio.

A. Eggs in the supermarket are graded as small, medium, large and jumbo
B. Employees are assigned identification numbers
C. Achievement motivation of hockey players
D. Players' height

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: B = Nominal (ID numbers are labels only). A = Ordinal (egg sizes have order but unequal intervals). C = Interval (achievement motivation scores have equal intervals but no true zero). D = Ratio (height has true zero and equal intervals).

questions.question:
One organisational psychologist wanted to verify the efficacy of a group based development intervention. For this purpose he undertook an Action Research. Suggest the correct sequence of the following components of his research.

A. Acting through the intervention
B. Observation
C. Planning about the intervention
D. Reflection

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Action research cycle (Lewin): (C) Planning the intervention → (A) Acting (implementing the intervention) → (B) Observing (collecting data on effects) → (D) Reflecting (evaluating and refining). Then the cycle repeats.

questions.question:
One psychologist has developed a tool on Nature connectedness. What would be correct sequence of the following psychometric activities.

A. Carrying out Exploratory Factor Analysis
B. Establishing Percentile Norm
C. Examining Croanbach Alfa
D. Verifying Predictive Validity
E. Establishing Content Validity

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Psychometric development sequence: (E) Content validity first → (C) Reliability (Cronbach's alpha) → (A) Factor analysis (structure) → (B) Norm establishment → (D) Predictive validity (requires established norms and time for criterion data).

questions.question:
Place the components of 'Broaden-and- Build model of Positive Emotion' in correct sequence

A. Building Enduring personal resources
B. Positive Emotions
C. Enhanced Health Fulfillments
D. Novel thoughts, Activities, Relationships

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Fredrickson's Broaden-and-Build sequence: (B) Positive emotions → (D) Broaden thought-action repertoires (novel thoughts, activities, relationships) → (A) Build enduring personal resources → (C) Enhanced health and fulfillment.

questions.question:
Arrange the following literary works on different facets of 'Yoga' in chronological order.

A. 'Anashshakti Yoga' by Mahatma Gandhi
B. 'Gitarahasya' by B.G. Tilak
C. 'Gatha' by Tukaram
D. 'Upadesha' by Raman Maharishi

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Chronological order: Tukaram's Gatha (17th century, ~1608-1649) → Ramana Maharishi's Upadesha (early 20th century, ~1900s) → Tilak's Gitarahasya (Karmayoga, 1915) → Gandhi's Anashshakti Yoga (1929).

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct?

A. Internal locus of control enhances the perception of stress
B. Stress functions as a motivator
C. The behavioural indicators of stress in children are seen in cognitive abilities, social competence and academic performance
D. In resistance stage of General Adaptation Syndrome (GAS), the physiological arousal peaks up to the all time high
E. Neglect, Victimization, Physical assault constitute toxic stress for children

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Moderate stress can be motivating (B). Children's stress manifests in cognitive, social, and academic domains (C). Neglect, victimization, and physical assault create toxic stress (E). Internal locus of control reduces stress perception (A is wrong). Physiological arousal peaks at Alarm stage, not Resistance (D is wrong).

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct?

A. Emotionally arousing stimuli have also been seen to lead to amnesia
B. Some cognitive processing must occur before an individual can experience an emotional response to an event
C. Repression is a form of motivated forgetting
D. Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) and Position Emission Topography (PET) are invasive scanning techniques of studying the brain functioning
E. Theories of emotions have not changed much over the years

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Emotional arousal can cause amnesia (A — emotional Stroop, weapon focus). Cognitive appraisal is needed for emotion (B — Lazarus). Repression is motivated forgetting (C — Freud). fMRI and PET are non-invasive (D is wrong). Emotion theories have evolved significantly (E is wrong).

questions.question:
Richardson's Resilience model refers to which of the following?

A. Reintegration with a loss
B. Resistance index
C. Biopsychospiritual homeostasis
D. Disruption
E. Outcome Index

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Richardson's (2002) resilience model includes: Biopsychospiritual homeostasis (C), Disruption from life events (D), and possible outcomes including Reintegration with loss (A), resilient reintegration, or dysfunctional reintegration.

questions.question:
Pineal Gland

A. Helps increase the blood calcium level
B. Secretes a hormone called 'melatonin'
C. Is located in epithalamus
D. Secretes hormones called 'parathormone' and 'calcitonin'
E. Is used to be known as the 'Third eye'

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: The pineal gland secretes melatonin (B), is located in the epithalamus (C), and was historically called the 'third eye' (E) due to its photosensitive properties. Parathormone and calcitonin are secreted by parathyroid and thyroid glands respectively (D and A are wrong).

questions.question:
Reality Therapy in counselling

A. Is based on principles of choice
B. Emphasises self-evaluation
C. Focuses on the way we live and exist
D. Views empowerment from a strength-based perspective
E. Follows the stages of Wants, Direction, Evaluation and Planning (WDEP)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Reality Therapy (William Glasser) is based on Choice Theory (A), emphasizes self-evaluation (B), and uses the WDEP system — Wants, Direction, Evaluation, Planning (E). It focuses on present behavior, not existential living (C).

questions.question:
Five ways to be proactive includes the following

A. Predict
B. Prevent
C. Program
D. Plan
E. Participate

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: The five P's of proactive coping are: Predict, Prevent, Plan, Participate, and Perform. Since 'Perform' is not among the options, the correct set is Predict (A), Prevent (B), Plan (D), and Participate (E). 'Program' (C) is not one of the standard Five Ps.

questions.question:
Which of the following are included in Bruner's theory of cognitive development?

A. Enactive
B. Echoic
C. Iconic
D. Symbolic
E. Deontic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Bruner's (1966) three modes of representation: Enactive (action-based, motor), Iconic (image-based, visual), and Symbolic (language-based, abstract). Echoic is sensory memory; deontic relates to obligation/logic.

questions.question:
Which of the following are not true about the differences between simple regression and multiple regression?

A. The number of predictors
B. The number of criteria
C. Coefficient of determination
D. Sample size

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: The key difference between simple and multiple regression is the number of predictors (A — true difference). Both have one criterion (B — NOT a difference). Coefficient of determination applies to both (C — NOT a difference in concept). Sample size requirements differ but aren't a fundamental structural difference (D — NOT a defining difference). The question asks what is NOT true about differences.

questions.question:
Which of the following terms are associated with Gestalt approach

A. Molar
B. Nativistic
C. Atomistic, Elementistic
D. Cognitive, Phenomenological
E. Objective

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Gestalt psychology is associated with: Molar (whole units, not molecular/atomistic — A), Nativistic (perceptual organization is innate — B), and Cognitive/Phenomenological (D). It opposes atomistic/elementistic approaches (C). It uses subjective methods, not purely objective (E).

questions.question:
Which one of the following are the reasons for forgetting?

A. The information is not attended to and fails to be encoded
B. Information accessed repeatedly decays
C. Older information in memory interfere with the learning of new information
D. Newer information interferes with the retrieval of older information
E. Information attended and perception is poor

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Forgetting occurs due to: Encoding failure (A — not attended), Proactive interference (C — old interferes with new), and Retroactive interference (D — new interferes with old). Decay theory is largely discredited (B is debatable). Poor perception with attended information (E) is not a standard cause.

questions.question:
Which of the following are community based protective factors for resilience among children

A. Ties to pro-social organisations
B. Authoritative parenting
C. Organised home environment
D. Neighborhood with high collective efficacy
E. Effective schools

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Community-level protective factors: Ties to pro-social organizations (A), neighborhood collective efficacy (D), and effective schools (E). Authoritative parenting (B) and organized home environment (C) are family-level factors, not community-based.

questions.question:
Which of the following methods can be used to determine the number of factors to be extracted in Exploratory Factor Analysis:

A. Liserel Analysis
B. Scree Test
C. Eigen value criteria
D. Rotation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: The Scree Test (Cattell — plot of eigenvalues) and Eigenvalue > 1 criterion (Kaiser-Guttman) are methods for determining the number of factors to extract. LISREL is CFA software; rotation is applied after extraction, not for determining factor count.

questions.question:
Which of the following softwares can be more helpful for analysis in qualitative research by a psychologist?

A. SPSS
B. AMOS
C. NVIVO
D. ATLAS
E. R

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: NVivo and ATLAS.ti are specialized qualitative data analysis (QDA) software for coding and analyzing textual/visual data. SPSS, AMOS, and R are quantitative analysis tools.

questions.question:
Which of the following refer to Advanced Empathy as per the Developmental Model of Counselling?

A. Confrontive challenging
B. Theme identification
C. Connecting islands
D. Making the implicit explicit
E. Fortune telling

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Advanced empathy in Egan's model involves: Theme identification (B — recognizing underlying patterns), Connecting islands (C — linking fragmented client expressions), and Making the implicit explicit (D — articulating unspoken feelings). Confrontation and fortune-telling are separate skills.

questions.question:
Which of the following are methods used in challenging in counselling as per the Developmental model of Egan?

A. Reviewing better times
B. Asocial response
C. Identification of models
D. Immediacy
E. Self-disclosure

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Egan's challenging methods include: Reviewing better times (A — recalling when things worked), Immediacy (D — addressing here-and-now relationship dynamics), and Self-disclosure (E — sharing counselor's experience). Asocial response and model identification are not standard challenging methods.

questions.question:
Which of the following are included in the steps of Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy?

A. Assessment
B. Cognitive restructuring
C. Installation
D. Skill Acquisition
E. Body scan

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Shapiro's 8-phase EMDR includes: Assessment (Phase 3), Installation of positive cognition (Phase 5), and Body scan (Phase 6). Cognitive restructuring is a CBT technique, not an EMDR phase. Skill acquisition is part of DBT/CBT, not standard EMDR.

questions.question:
Which of the following refer to the theories of Health Behaviour?

A. Reflection-Action Theory
B. Protective Motivation Theory
C. Dialectical Behavioural Theory
D. Precaution Adoption Process Model
E. Organismic Integration Theory

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Protective Motivation Theory (Rogers — B), Precaution Adoption Process Model (Weinstein — D), and Organismic Integration Theory (part of SDT applied to health — E) are health behavior theories. Dialectical Behavior Therapy is a clinical intervention (C), not a health behavior theory.

questions.question:
Which of the following are characteristics of a good Hypothesis?

A. Affirmative statement
B. Interrogative statement
C. Falsifiability
D. Conjectural
E. Concludes relationship between variables

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: A good hypothesis is: a declarative/affirmative statement (A, not interrogative), falsifiable/testable (C), and conjectural/tentative (D). It states relationships between variables but doesn't 'conclude' them (E — conclusions come after testing).

questions.question:
Which of the following are measures of dispersion?

A. Standard Deviation
B. Quartile Deviation
C. Mode
D. Variance
E. Range

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: Measures of dispersion include: Standard Deviation (A), Quartile Deviation (B), Variance (D), and Range (E). Mode (C) is a measure of central tendency, not dispersion.

questions.question:
Advaita Vedanta asserts that sensory knowledge is ____

A. Illusionary
B. Absolutely false
C. Possible in a transcendental state
D. Relatively true, but not absolutely true

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.concept: According to Advaita Vedanta (Shankara), sensory knowledge is illusionary/maya (A) and relatively true at the empirical level (vyavaharika) but not absolutely true at the transcendental level (paramarthika) (D). It is not 'absolutely false' as it has empirical validity.

questions.concept: Drive-Reduction Theory by Hull (A-IV). Personality and Need for Achievement (nAch) — Carol Dweck's work on mindset relates to achievement motivation (B-III). Arousal Theory by Yerkes-Dodson (C-I). Self-Determination Theory by Ryan and Deci (D-II).

questions.concept: Sage Bharata's Natya Shastra classifies Bhavas (emotions): Krodha = Anger (A-III), Bhaya = Fear (B-IV), Jugupsa = Disgust (C-I), Vismaya = Wonder/Astonishment (D-II).

questions.concept: Hypothalamus regulates temperature, thirst, hunger (A-II). Hippocampus forms long-term declarative memories (B-III). Amygdala processes fear responses and fear memory (C-I). Cingulate cortex is involved in selective attention and working memory (D-IV).

questions.question:

questions.concept: Gestalt Therapy uses the empty chair technique (A-III). Reality Therapy/Glasser's Choice Theory emphasizes five basic needs (B-I). Existentialism views the individual as architect of their own life (C-II). Solution-Focused Brief Therapy was developed by de Shazer and Berg (D-IV).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Art Therapy is used for emotional expression/release (C-IV). Existentialism deals with life's paradoxes (death, freedom, isolation, meaninglessness — D-II).

content.heading: Comprehension Passage 1 (Questions 91–95)
content.text: The researchers assumed that older adults are different from younger adults in their suicidal ideation and in their reasons for thinking about committing suicide because of differences in life experiences and coping competence. Hence, they used cross sectional research and recruited 150 older adults (60-95 years) who were matched with 150 younger adult (17-34 years) on gender ethnicity, religion and self reported health status. Beck's scale for suicidal ideation was used to measure suicidal ideation. They used 't' test for comparison of variables and found no significant difference. According to Siegler, neither cross sectional nor longitudinal study provide much information about how those changes occur over time. He discussed a method that involves carefully observing behavior during periods when rapid change is occurring and collecting both quantitative and qualitative information.

questions.question: A potential problem with cross sectional research is that there may be other variables that are confounded with age. This problem is called
questions.concept: The cohort effect is a confound in cross-sectional designs where differences between age groups may be due to generational/cohort differences (historical experiences, culture) rather than age itself.

questions.question: The combination of cross sectional and longitudinal research is called
questions.concept: Sequential research (Schaie, 1965) combines cross-sectional and longitudinal approaches by following multiple cohorts over time, allowing separation of age, cohort, and period effects.

questions.question: What is the df for the 't' test used here
questions.concept: For an independent samples t-test: df = n1 + n2 - 2 = 150 + 150 - 2 = 298.

questions.question: What is the method Siegler discussed for studying the process of change?
questions.concept: The microgenetic method (Siegler, 1996) involves intensive observation of behavior during periods of rapid change, collecting both quantitative and qualitative data to understand how developmental changes occur in real time.

questions.question: When null hypothesis is false and we are accepting it then we make
questions.subtopic: Type I and Type II Errors
questions.concept: A Type II error (β) occurs when we fail to reject a false null hypothesis — accepting H₀ when it is actually false. Type I error is rejecting a true null hypothesis.

content.heading: Comprehension Passage 2 (Questions 96–100)
content.text: Motivation is the driving force behind human activities. Researchers identified three components of motivation. Motivation originates externally or internally, are defined by action or non-action and can be categorized as extrinsic, identified, intrinsic, or introjected. One of the causes of flow motivation is "just because an approach or method worked for someone else does not mean that it will work for you". Self-determination theory is built on the idea that people are actively motivated to pursue their goals.

questions.question: What are the three components of motivation?
questions.concept: The three components of motivation are: Activation (initiating behavior), Persistence (sustaining effort over time), and Intensity (concentration and vigor of effort).

questions.question: What are the components of intrinsic motivation?
questions.concept: Intrinsic motivation is driven by Autonomy (sense of choice), Mastery (desire to improve skills), and Purpose (meaningful goals). These align with Self-Determination Theory's basic needs (autonomy, competence) plus the additional element of purpose.

questions.question: "Just because an approach or method worked for someone else does not mean that it will work for you" refers to
options: (C) there is no common approach for all
(D) the approach will work for me
questions.concept: This statement challenges the 'one size fits all' assumption in motivation — what motivates one person may not motivate another due to individual differences in needs, goals, and contexts.

questions.question: Introjected motivation is
questions.concept: In SDT's continuum of motivation, introjected regulation involves internalizing external pressures (guilt, shame, ego-involvement) without full acceptance. It is negative because it creates internal conflict and anxiety rather than genuine volition.

questions.question: Self determination theory is developed by:
questions.concept: Self-Determination Theory (SDT) was developed by Edward Deci and Richard Ryan. It proposes three basic psychological needs — autonomy, competence, and relatedness — whose satisfaction is essential for intrinsic motivation and wellbeing.
